claims.sentence: You need computing devices such as a desktop computer, laptop, or tablet to take a remote assessment
You must have communication equipment that provides access to the university's electronic educational environment through local networks and the Internet
You must also have the corresponding software installed
If a course page specifies technical requirements that differ from or go beyond this official document, the official document takes precedence
If your assessment uses video conferencing, you should use a webcam with a resolution of at least 640x480 (0.3 MP)
You should use a monitor or screen with a resolution of at least 1280x1024
You need a microphone with speakers or a computer headset for communication
You need configured video conferencing software such as Microsoft Teams, Zoom, or a similar program that allows remote audio-visual contact
Your internet connection speed must be at least 2 Mbps, or 1024 Kbps per workstation
You must use the Google Chrome browser, version 81.0 or higher
For assessments using a proctoring system, you should use the Google Chrome browser, version 72 or higher
Your operating system must be at least Windows 7, macOS 10.12 Sierra, or Linux
You should use a webcam with a resolution of at least 640x480 (0.3 MP)
You need a microphone with speakers or a computer headset to communicate with the proctor
Your internet connection speed must be at least 512 Kbps
A browser plugin may be required if necessary
For online testing, you should use the Google Chrome browser, version 72 or higher
Your operating system must be at least Windows 7, macOS 10.12 Sierra, or Linux
Your internet connection speed must be at least 512 Kbps
If your assessment uses a format chosen independently by the instructor, the instructor sets the technical and software requirements and recommendations
You must receive these requirements no later than 3 working days before the assessment day
The notification is sent via corporate email addresses and/or other information and communication technologies
The evidence does not specify which software is required for general access to the electronic educational environment
The evidence does not list operating system requirements for the general setup or for video conferencing mode
The evidence does not state what happens if a student's equipment does not meet the recommended specifications
The evidence does not define what constitutes other information and communication technologies for notifications
The evidence does not specify which browser plugins are needed for proctoring beyond stating they may be required
Course pages may list different or additional technical requirements; if they do, the official document takes precedence
The evidence leaves open whether the recommended specifications are mandatory or optional for each format
